summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with rectal bleeding and abdominal pain radiating to the chest, in the context of chronic alcohol use, tobacco dependence, and known esophageal reflux. Evaluation confirmed guaiac-positive stool and anemia of chronic disease, with no infectious cause found on stool testing. Imaging from a recent admission showed findings consistent with alcoholic liver damage, esophageal thickening, and significant periportal lymphadenopathy. The patient was stabilized without intervention, and the bleeding subsided during the short stay. He was discharged with plans for gastroenterology follow-up, management of anemia, and referrals for alcohol and tobacco use counseling. Microscopic hematuria was incidentally noted but deemed non-urgent.
problems: Other and unspecified noninfectious gastroenteritis and colitis
